title: Auth — OOB Redeem — payload
description: The starter turns an approved out-of-band request into the outcome its purpose defines — for `login`, a session bound to the starter key; for `deviceEnrol`, an ACL entry whose subject is the starter key. Issued and signed by the starter key; held as a long poll until the request is approved. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

Response.title: Auth — OOB Redeem — response payload
Response.description: For `login`: who is now signed in, for the starter's "Continue as …?" confirmation. Never tokens: over HTTPS the session itself is delivered as HttpOnly cookies. For `deviceEnrol`: the VTA, the ACL entry it created for the starter key, and when that key must be swapped out. Exactly one of the two shapes.

subject.description: `login` only. The approving DID — the grant's issuer — now the session's subject.

displayName.description: `login` only. A name for the signed-in identity, for the confirmation step. Untrusted wherever rendered.

sessionEndsAt.description: `login` only. When the session ends, as an RFC 3339 date-time: the earlier of the grant's `sessionEndsAt` and the service's session limit.

amr.description: `login` only. Authentication Methods References (RFC 8176) for the session. For this family: `["did", "oob", "uv"]`.

vtaDid.description: `deviceEnrol` only: the DID of the VTA the client is now enrolled at — the service, and the `issuer` of this response.

aclEntry.description: `deviceEnrol` only: the ACL entry the VTA created, as acl/show would return it. Its `subject` is the starter key until the client swaps it; its scope is the grant's `aclScope`; its `delegatedBy` is the grant's issuer.

swapClosesAt.description: `deviceEnrol` only: the instant by which the client must replace the starter key with its own DID through acl/swap-key, as an RFC 3339 date-time. At most 300 s after the redeem; the VTA removes the entry if it has not been swapped by then.
